deep.reconstruction:
The page is printed p. 9 of an elementary arithmetic textbook. The bundle name 'HB.Leiste' suggests Christian Leiste's 'Arithmetik und Algebra' (Wolfenbüttel, c.1790), which Gauss would have used as a schoolboy. On it are a few handwritten corrections and some marginal scribbles bleeding in from the facing page. Section by section, the printed text says:

§11: The multiplication table ('Einmal Eins', attributed to Pythagoras) lists the products of all single digits taken pairwise. By §10 it can be built by repeated addition: n*m = m + m + ... + m (n times).

§12: Commutativity of multiplication, read off the rectangular array of points or lines in §9. Four taken six times equals six taken four times. In symbols A*B = B*A.

§13: The factors may themselves be products. Example: A = 4 = 2*2 and B = 6 = 3*2. In general, with A = ab and B = cd, AB = BA = abcd = cdab, and the factors may be permuted further. The book's chain is 4*6 = 2*2*3*2 = 2*2*2*3 = 24. This is generalized commutativity and associativity. A note (Anmerk.) says the multiplication dot is required between numerals but is omitted between lower-case letters.

§14: Division is defined as a 'geometric ratio' of divisor to dividend. The quotient, also called the exponent of the ratio, says how many times the divisor is contained in the dividend. It is written 24:4 = 24/4 = 6. Division can also be pictured as repeated subtraction of the divisor from the dividend; the number of possible subtractions is the quotient (24-4-4-4-4-4-4 = 0, six times). The print wrongly says 'from the quotient'. A hand has struck 'Quotienten' and written 'Dividendus' in the right margin.

§15 (misprinted as a second §14; corrected by hand to 15): The divisor is contained in the dividend as often as unity is in the quotient, i.e. 4:24 = 1:6, i.e. 24/4 = 6/1. The factors of §9 become divisor and quotient, and the dividend is their product. This continues on p. 10 as 24/4 = 4*6/4, with multiplication serving as the check of division.

Left margin: fragments of Gauss's handwriting from the facing page (p. 8). They belong to his computations there: '1.2.3.4' with a fraction from the alternating series N = a^nA - b^nB/(1.2) + ..., '=0', '= hh+3M' (or 3l), '29.7 = A^2', '553', '676'. There is also an illegible note near §13. None of this constitutes a derivation on this page.
errors: Printed text: division described as repeated subtraction of the divisor 'vom Quotienten' (from the quotient). This should be 'from the dividend'. It is correctly emended by hand in the margin to 'Dividendus'.
Printed text: section number '§. 14' is duplicated; the second should be §15. It is corrected by hand, which is consistent with §16 on the next page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of a printed elementary schoolbook (likely Leiste's arithmetic). The only handwritten content is the correction of an obvious misprint ('Quotienten' to 'Dividendus'), a renumbering of a section, and stray margin fragments from the facing page. There is no mathematical content attributable to Gauss beyond proofreading.

checkable.asserts: Division as repeated subtraction of the divisor from the dividend (6 subtractions)

transcription_corrections: The handwritten marginal correction reads 'Dividen-du[s]' (written as 'Dividen' / 'du' across two lines) beside the struck-through 'Quotienten'.
The section number is printed '§. 14' (a duplicate) with a handwritten '5' overwriting the 4, giving §15.

The left-margin items belong to Gauss's notes on the facing page 8, not to this page. The reading '9.7 = d^2' is more likely '29.7 = 𝔄^2', cut off by the gutter, matching the previous page. '= hh + 3l' is likely '= hh + 3M'.
There is an illegible handwritten note in the left margin beside §13 (roughly '...zög... bey Ae po...'), which is omitted in the transcription.
